scope: Independent review of producer support-gap handoff and actual three-node transport; consumer implementation separately reviewed by root.

findings_resolved.issue: Final READY registration could cross original support-gap ROS/monotonic cutoff while waiting for commit lock.
findings_resolved.resolution: Within original input_lock, immediately before new registration creation, producer rechecks immutable support receipt and original monotonic cutoff. Both independently injected post-proof expiry cases pass.

review_notes: Station-specific branch follows original seven-class support missing/positive-conflict/provenance gate; initial or unregistered station retains original path.

Actual current frame and complete existing station registration are required, plus exact RGB-D, unchanged frozen owner/source/config/epoch, real current stationary feedback. No ordinary locked-source pending is created and no old geometry or plan is reused.
Gap receipt and monotonic cap remain fixed to original parent geometry/identity/phase/session earliest deadline. Repeated failed frames retain first-source and original clocks.
Current independent support, unique candidate and RGB identity proof are mandatory before full fresh recovery. Marker and clocks are rechecked before registration commit.

Three-node regression uses actual producer image/segmentation/recovery and both task/remote ingress, including invalid geometry callback, three-message ordering, READY-before-pending, late old notifications, deadline, manual takeover and real target loss.

Fixture is an exact copy of independently extracted GEN19 statuses. Recorded recovery lacks station contract because original task retired; synthetic full-chain recovery is explicitly separate and does not claim replay of a historical repaired trial.
limitations: No live ROS, hardware motion, trajectory acceptance, or physical grasp success was performed by this review.
Consumer helper/task/remote sources are not independently reviewed here because this reviewer authored them; root_consumer_review.json covers those four changed files.
